newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 29.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- CITIC Pacific has extended its reach in Hong Kong's key industries by buying a 20 per cent stake in China Light & Power.
-- Beijing sources say China's leaders have given out instructions that Hong Kong must not be allowed to be used by foreign anti-China forces and become an anti-Communist city.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recommended banks cut mortgages lent to luxury home buyers from 70 to 60 percent of a property's value. Analysts said foreign and Chinese banks would be affected more by the decision.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Next month souvenirs commemorating the handover will flood markets in China, Hong Kong and overseas. The Association for the Celebration of Reunification of Hong Kong with China revealed plans for 180 commemorative goods. The right to make these souvenirs with the dolphin logo of the Association, had been given to an American company.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin said Sino-U.S. relations had good prospects when he met a delegation of senior officials of the California state government.
-- The Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said he had decided to postpone the announcement of his cabinet list until after the Chinese Lunar New Year holiday.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Legislators will be bombarded with horror stories from the music and entertainment industry when they debate the Copyright Bill in the Legislative Council on Wednesday. The local music industry will say the bill will strangle them, causing closures and job losses.

-- As China stepped up its purchase of U.S. Treasury bills, it could soon overtake Japan as the biggest foreign owners of U.S. financial notes. And the trend would only strengthen when Hong Kong returned to China with its hefty chunk of U.S. bonds.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Guangzhou is eager to maintain its car manufacturing status by attracting foreign investment after a Peugeot project turned sour.
-- Market sources say prime office rents in Shanghai have tumbled 30 percent in the past year and are set to fall 15 per cent more this year.
